<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-potentially-unwanted-applications-pua-protection-md"></div>

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-potentially-unwanted-applications-pua-protection-md-req-paw-058-configure-potentially-unwanted-applications-pua-protection-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-058] Configure Potentially Unwanted Applications (PUA) Protection for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-potentially-unwanted-applications-pua-protection-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-potentially-unwanted-applications-pua-protection-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender`
      * `PUAProtection` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-potentially-unwanted-applications-pua-protection-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Potentially Unwanted Applications (PUA) include adware, torrent clients, cryptominers, and system optimizers that increase risk and resource consumption. Forcing PUA blocking stops standard vectors of shadow IT and unauthorized utility tool execution.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-potentially-unwanted-applications-pua-protection-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Legitimate but unrecognized administrative utilities may be blocked. Standard exclusions must be configured for approved utilities.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-potentially-unwanted-applications-pua-protection-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-potentially-unwanted-applications-pua-protection-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus
2. Set 'Configure detection for potentially unwanted applications' to 'Enabled'
3. Select 'Block' in the options dropdown list

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-potentially-unwanted-applications-pua-protection-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-PawDefenderPUA.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-PawDefenderPUA.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-PawDefenderPUA.ps1
Set-MpPreference -PUAProtection 1
Set-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender" -Name "PUAProtection" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-PawDefenderPUAStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-PawDefenderPUAStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-PawDefenderPUAStatus.ps1
$Pref = Get-MpPreference
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender" -Name "PUAProtection" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($Pref.PUAProtection -eq 1 -or ($Reg -and $Reg.PUAProtection -eq 1)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-prevent-local-list-merging-and-exclusions-configuration-md"></div>

<div id="07-paws-defender-prevent-local-list-merging-and-exclusions-configuration-md-req-paw-059-prevent-local-list-merging-and-exclusions-configuration-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-059] Prevent Local List Merging and Exclusions Configuration for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-prevent-local-list-merging-and-exclusions-configuration-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-prevent-local-list-merging-and-exclusions-configuration-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender`
      * `DisableLocalAdminMerge` = `1` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender`
      * `HideExclusionsFromLocalAdmins` = `1` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions`
      * `DisableLocalAdminConfiguration` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-prevent-local-list-merging-and-exclusions-configuration-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
If local administrators or compromised administrative accounts can modify Defender exclusions or merge local lists, they can authorize malicious folders or tools. Restricting list configuration to central GPOs ensures consistent security enforcement.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-prevent-local-list-merging-and-exclusions-configuration-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Local administrators will be unable to add folders or scripts to Defender exclusions. All exclusions must be managed centrally via GPO.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-prevent-local-list-merging-and-exclusions-configuration-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-prevent-local-list-merging-and-exclusions-configuration-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus
2. Set 'Configure local administrator merge behavior for lists' to 'Disabled'
3. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Exclusions
4. Set 'Prevent users from configuring exclusions' to 'Enabled'
5. Set 'Control whether or not exclusions are visible to Local Admins' to 'Enabled'

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-prevent-local-list-merging-and-exclusions-configuration-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-PawDefenderLocalExclusions.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-PawDefenderLocalExclusions.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-PawDefenderLocalExclusions.ps1
Set-MpPreference -DisableLocalAdminMerge $true
Set-MpPreference -DisableExclusionRestriction $false
$Path = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender"
if (-not (Test-Path $Path)) { New-Item -Path $Path -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $Path -Name "DisableLocalAdminMerge" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $Path -Name "HideExclusionsFromLocalAdmins" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
$ExclPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions"
if (-not (Test-Path $ExclPath)) { New-Item -Path $ExclPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ExclPath -Name "DisableLocalAdminConfiguration" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-PawDefenderLocalExclusionsStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-PawDefenderLocalExclusionsStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-PawDefenderLocalExclusionsStatus.ps1
$Pref = Get-MpPreference
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender" -Name "DisableLocalAdminMerge" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$RegHide = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender" -Name "HideExclusionsFromLocalAdmins" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$RegConfig = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions" -Name "DisableLocalAdminConfiguration" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if (($Pref.DisableLocalAdminMerge -eq $true -or ($Reg -and $Reg.DisableLocalAdminMerge -eq 1)) -and
    ($RegHide -and $RegHide.HideExclusionsFromLocalAdmins -eq 1) -and
    ($RegConfig -and $RegConfig.DisableLocalAdminConfiguration -eq 1)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-auto-exclusions-configuration-md-req-paw-060-configure-auto-exclusions-configuration-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-060] Configure Auto Exclusions Configuration for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-auto-exclusions-configuration-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-auto-exclusions-configuration-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Exclusions`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions`
      * `DisableAutoExclusions` = `0` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-auto-exclusions-configuration-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Auto Exclusions automatically configure exclusions for known safe system folders or server roles to reduce performance overhead. Enforcing that auto exclusions are not disabled ensures server performance stability and proper system scanning.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-auto-exclusions-configuration-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
None.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-auto-exclusions-configuration-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-auto-exclusions-configuration-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Exclusions
2. Set 'Turn off Auto Exclusions' to 'Disabled'

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-auto-exclusions-configuration-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-PawDefenderAutoExclusions.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-PawDefenderAutoExclusions.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-PawDefenderAutoExclusions.ps1
$ExclPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions"
if (-not (Test-Path $ExclPath)) { New-Item -Path $ExclPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ExclPath -Name "DisableAutoExclusions" -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-PawDefenderAutoExclusionsStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-PawDefenderAutoExclusionsStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-PawDefenderAutoExclusionsStatus.ps1
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions" -Name "DisableAutoExclusions" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($Reg -and $Reg.DisableAutoExclusions -eq 0) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-edr-in-block-mode-md-req-paw-061-enable-edr-in-block-mode-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-061] Enable EDR in Block Mode for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-edr-in-block-mode-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-edr-in-block-mode-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Features`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Features`
      * `PassiveRemediation` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-edr-in-block-mode-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) in Block Mode allows Defender to take remediation actions on malicious artifacts detected by Microsoft Defender for Endpoint even if another non-Microsoft antivirus is primary. This establishes secondary defensive block capabilities.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-edr-in-block-mode-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
None. Extends passive monitoring to execute block operations when necessary.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-edr-in-block-mode-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-edr-in-block-mode-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Features
2. Set 'Enable EDR in block mode' to 'Enabled'

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-edr-in-block-mode-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-PawDefenderEdrBlockMode.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-PawDefenderEdrBlockMode.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-PawDefenderEdrBlockMode.ps1
$FeaturesPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Features"
if (-not (Test-Path $FeaturesPath)) { New-Item -Path $FeaturesPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $FeaturesPath -Name "PassiveRemediation" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-PawDefenderEdrBlockModeStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-PawDefenderEdrBlockModeStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-PawDefenderEdrBlockModeStatus.ps1
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Features" -Name "PassiveRemediation" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($Reg -and $Reg.PassiveRemediation -eq 1) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-allow-network-protection-on-windows-server-md-req-paw-062-allow-network-protection-on-windows-server-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-062] Allow Network Protection on Windows Server for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-allow-network-protection-on-windows-server-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-allow-network-protection-on-windows-server-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Network Protection`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Network Protection`
      * `AllowNetworkProtectionOnWinServer` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-allow-network-protection-on-windows-server-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Network Protection blocks processes from accessing malicious domains, phishing sites, and host IP ranges. Allowing Network Protection on Windows Server ensures that member servers running server workloads possess the same IP filter protections as client platforms.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-allow-network-protection-on-windows-server-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Unrecognized or legacy client-server connections to custom web resources may be filtered. Exclusions must be mapped under DFE.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-allow-network-protection-on-windows-server-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-allow-network-protection-on-windows-server-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Network Protection
2. Set 'This setting controls whether Network Protection is allowed to be configured into block or audit mode on Windows Server' to 'Enabled'

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-allow-network-protection-on-windows-server-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-PawDefenderNetworkProtectionServer.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-PawDefenderNetworkProtectionServer.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-PawDefenderNetworkProtectionServer.ps1
$NetProtPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Network Protection"
if (-not (Test-Path $NetProtPath)) { New-Item -Path $NetProtPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $NetProtPath -Name "AllowNetworkProtectionOnWinServer" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-PawDefenderNetworkProtectionServerStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-PawDefenderNetworkProtectionServerStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-PawDefenderNetworkProtectionServerStatus.ps1
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Network Protection" -Name "AllowNetworkProtectionOnWinServer" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-file-hash-computation-md-req-paw-063-enable-file-hash-computation-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-063] Enable File Hash Computation for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-file-hash-computation-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-file-hash-computation-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\MpEngine`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\MpEngine`
      * `EnableFileHashComputation` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-file-hash-computation-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Computing cryptographic file hashes allows Defender to pass hashes of scanned files to cloud and SIEM PAW platforms. This enables precise IOC matches, file tracking, and correlation with threat intelligence repositories.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-file-hash-computation-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Minor CPU/Disk I/O impact when scanning large directories.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-file-hash-computation-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-file-hash-computation-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\MpEngine
2. Set 'Enable file hash computation feature' to 'Enabled'

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-file-hash-computation-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-PawDefenderFileHash.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-PawDefenderFileHash.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-PawDefenderFileHash.ps1
Set-MpPreference -EnableFileHashComputation $true
$MpEnginePath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\MpEngine"
if (-not (Test-Path $MpEnginePath)) { New-Item -Path $MpEnginePath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $MpEnginePath -Name "EnableFileHashComputation" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-PawDefenderFileHashStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-PawDefenderFileHashStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-PawDefenderFileHashStatus.ps1
$Pref = Get-MpPreference
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\MpEngine" -Name "EnableFileHashComputation" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($Pref.EnableFileHashComputation -eq $true -or ($Reg -and $Reg.EnableFileHashComputation -eq 1)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md"></div>

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-req-paw-064-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-064] Configure Network Inspection System (NIS) settings for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Network Inspection System`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\NIS`
      * `EnableConvertWarnToBlock` = `1` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\NIS`
      * `AllowSwitchToAsyncInspection` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
The Network Inspection System (NIS) inspects network traffic patterns for known exploits. Converting warning verdicts to block enforces inline blocking of zero-day exploits, while allowing async inspection prevents performance overhead from slowing local network interfaces.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
None.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Network Inspection System
2. Set 'Convert warn verdict to block' to 'Enabled'
3. Set 'Turn on asynchronous inspection' to 'Enabled'

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-network-inspection-system-nis-settings-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-PawDefenderNis.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-PawDefenderNis.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-PawDefenderNis.ps1
$NisPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\NIS"
if (-not (Test-Path $NisPath)) { New-Item -Path $NisPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $NisPath -Name "EnableConvertWarnToBlock" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $NisPath -Name "AllowSwitchToAsyncInspection" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-PawDefenderNisStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-PawDefenderNisStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-PawDefenderNisStatus.ps1
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\NIS" -Name "EnableConvertWarnToBlock" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$RegAsync = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\NIS" -Name "AllowSwitchToAsyncInspection" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if (($Reg -and $Reg.EnableConvertWarnToBlock -eq 1) -and ($RegAsync -and $RegAsync.AllowSwitchToAsyncInspection -eq 1)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-oobe-real-time-protection-and-security-intelligence-md"></div>

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-oobe-real-time-protection-and-security-intelligence-md-req-paw-065-configure-oobe-real-time-protection-and-security-intelligence-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-065] Configure OOBE Real-Time Protection and Security Intelligence for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-oobe-real-time-protection-and-security-intelligence-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-oobe-real-time-protection-and-security-intelligence-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Real-time Protection`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Real-Time Protection`
      * `OobeEnableRtpAndSigUpdate` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-oobe-real-time-protection-and-security-intelligence-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Enabling real-time protection and intelligence updates during the Out-of-Box Experience (OOBE) ensures that the system is fully updated and protected before the initial administrative user signs in or connects to enterprise network nodes.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-oobe-real-time-protection-and-security-intelligence-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Negligible. Minor network traffic during initial provisioning phases.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-oobe-real-time-protection-and-security-intelligence-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-oobe-real-time-protection-and-security-intelligence-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Real-time Protection
2. Set 'Configure real-time protection and Security Intelligence Updates during OOBE' to 'Enabled'

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-oobe-real-time-protection-and-security-intelligence-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-PawDefenderOobeRtp.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-PawDefenderOobeRtp.ps1)


<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-req-paw-066-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-066] Enable Dynamic Signature Dropped Event Reporting for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Low
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Reporting`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Reporting`
      * `EnableDynamicSignatureDroppedEventReporting` = `1` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Enabling this log report generation triggers explicit events when a dynamic scan ruleset signature is dropped. This ensures SIEM integrations can immediately log changes in the local threat signatures dataset.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
None.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Reporting
2. Set 'Configure whether to report Dynamic Signature dropped events' to 'Enabled'

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-enable-dynamic-signature-dropped-event-reporting-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-PawDefenderDynamicReporting.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-PawDefenderDynamicReporting.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-PawDefenderDynamicReporting.ps1
$RepPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Reporting"
if (-not (Test-Path $RepPath)) { New-Item -Path $RepPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $RepPath -Name "EnableDynamicSignatureDroppedEventReporting" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-PawDefenderDynamicReportingStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-PawDefenderDynamicReportingStatus.ps1)

```powershell

    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md"></div>

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-req-paw-067-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-067] Configure Quick Scan and Scanning Exclusions for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Scan`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan`
      * `QuickScanIncludeExclusions` = `1` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan`
      * `DisablePackedExeScanning` = `0` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Malware frequently tries to establish persistence in excluded directories or inside packed/compressed executables. Forcing quick scans to include excluded files and ensuring packed file structures are recursively scanned prevents malware evasion.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Increased quick scan times depending on folder sizes and compression ratios.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Scan
2. Set 'Scan excluded files and directories during quick scans' to 'Enabled'
3. Set 'Turn off scanning of packed executables' to 'Disabled'

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-quick-scan-and-scanning-exclusions-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-PawDefenderQuickScan.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-PawDefenderQuickScan.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-PawDefenderQuickScan.ps1
Set-MpPreference -DisablePackedExeScanning $false
$ScanPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan"
if (-not (Test-Path $ScanPath)) { New-Item -Path $ScanPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ScanPath -Name "QuickScanIncludeExclusions" -Value 1 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ScanPath -Name "DisablePackedExeScanning" -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-PawDefenderQuickScanStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-PawDefenderQuickScanStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-PawDefenderQuickScanStatus.ps1
$Pref = Get-MpPreference
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan" -Name "QuickScanIncludeExclusions" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$RegPack = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan" -Name "DisablePackedExeScanning" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if (($Pref.DisablePackedExeScanning -eq $false -or ($RegPack -and $RegPack.DisablePackedExeScanning -eq 0)) -and
    ($Reg -and $Reg.QuickScanIncludeExclusions -eq 1)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-req-paw-068-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-068] Configure Scheduled Scan Parameters for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Scan`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan`
      * `ScheduleDay` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan`
      * `DisableEmailScanning` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan`
      * `DisableHeuristics` = `0` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan`
      * `DaysWithoutCatchupQuickScan` = `7` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Ensuring daily scheduled scans, enabling heuristics for behavioral anomaly detection, scan mail attachments, and forcing a catchup scan after at most 7 days ensures system integrity is continually validated.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Slight scanning overhead.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Scan
2. Set 'Specify the day of the week to run a scheduled scan' to 'Enabled' (Select 'Every day' or '0')
3. Set 'Turn on e-mail scanning' to 'Enabled'
4. Set 'Turn on heuristics' to 'Enabled'
5. Set 'Trigger a quick scan after X days without any scans' to 'Enabled' (7 days)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-scheduled-scan-parameters-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-PawDefenderScheduledScan.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-PawDefenderScheduledScan.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-PawDefenderScheduledScan.ps1
Set-MpPreference -DisableEmailScanning $false
Set-MpPreference -DisableHeuristics $false
$ScanPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan"
if (-not (Test-Path $ScanPath)) { New-Item -Path $ScanPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ScanPath -Name "ScheduleDay" -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ScanPath -Name "DisableEmailScanning" -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ScanPath -Name "DisableHeuristics" -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $ScanPath -Name "DaysWithoutCatchupQuickScan" -Value 7 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-PawDefenderScheduledScanStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-PawDefenderScheduledScanStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-PawDefenderScheduledScanStatus.ps1
$Pref = Get-MpPreference
$RegDays = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Scan" -Name "DaysWithoutCatchupQuickScan" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($Pref.DisableEmailScanning -eq $false -and $Pref.DisableHeuristics -eq $false -and ($RegDays -and $RegDays.DaysWithoutCatchupQuickScan -eq 7)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-req-paw-069-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-069] Configure Security Intelligence Update Schedule for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: Medium
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Security Intelligence Updates`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates`
      * `ASSignatureDue` = `7` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates`
      * `AVSignatureDue` = `7` (REG_DWORD)
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates`
      * `ScheduleDay` = `0` (REG_DWORD)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Antivirus signatures must remain fresh to block the latest published threats. Mandating daily checks for updates and marking signatures older than 7 days as out-of-date ensures continuous defense parity.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Requires continuous outbound connectivity to WSUS or Microsoft Update endpoints.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Security Intelligence Updates
2. Set 'Define the number of days before spyware security intelligence is considered out of date' to 'Enabled' (7 days)
3. Set 'Define the number of days before virus security intelligence is considered out of date' to 'Enabled' (7 days)
4. Set 'Specify the day of the week to check for security intelligence updates' to 'Enabled' (Every day or 0)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-security-intelligence-update-schedule-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-PawDefenderUpdateSchedule.ps1](../implementation_scripts/Configure-PawDefenderUpdateSchedule.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-PawDefenderUpdateSchedule.ps1
$SigPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates"
if (-not (Test-Path $SigPath)) { New-Item -Path $SigPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $SigPath -Name "ASSignatureDue" -Value 7 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $SigPath -Name "AVSignatureDue" -Value 7 -Type DWord -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path $SigPath -Name "ScheduleDay" -Value 0 -Type DWord -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-PawDefenderUpdateScheduleStatus.ps1](../audit_scripts/Get-PawDefenderUpdateScheduleStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-PawDefenderUpdateScheduleStatus.ps1
$Reg = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates" -Name "ASSignatureDue" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$RegAV = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates" -Name "AVSignatureDue" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$RegDay = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Signature Updates" -Name "ScheduleDay" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if (($Reg -and $Reg.ASSignatureDue -eq 7) -and ($RegAV -and $RegAV.AVSignatureDue -eq 7) -and ($RegDay -and $RegDay.ScheduleDay -eq 0)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md"></div>

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-for-paws"></div>
# Configure Attack Surface Reduction Rules for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules are critical for PAWs to enforce administrative isolation. Spawning tools from Office documents, dumping memory from LSASS, or launching WMI/PSExec child commands represent standard post-exploitation vectors.

This submodule contains individual requirement rules for each ASR control enforced on Privileged Access Workstations.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
* **Strict Block Enforcement**: Unlike standard workstations, all rules are enforced immediately in **Block** mode (`1`) as there should be no productive Office files, macros, or legacy scripts active on directory management consoles.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-configure-attack-surface-reduction-rules-md-enforced-attack-surface-reduction-rules-on-paws"></div>
## Enforced Attack Surface Reduction Rules on PAWs

The following individual ASR rules must be configured in Block mode:

1. **[REQ-PAW-076 - ASR: Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md)**
2. **[REQ-PAW-077 - ASR: Block Adobe Reader from creating child processes for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md)**
3. **[REQ-PAW-078 - ASR: Block all Office applications from creating child processes for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md)**
4. **[REQ-PAW-079 - ASR: Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md)**
5. **[REQ-PAW-080 - ASR: Block executable content from email client and webmail for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md)**
6. **[REQ-PAW-081 - ASR: Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-low-prevalence-executable-files-md)**
7. **[REQ-PAW-082 - ASR: Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md)**
8. **[REQ-PAW-083 - ASR: Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-script-launching-downloaded-content-md)**
9. **[REQ-PAW-084 - ASR: Block Office applications from creating executable content for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-executable-content-creation-md)**
10. **[REQ-PAW-085 - ASR: Block Office applications from injecting code into other processes for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-code-injection-md)**
11. **[REQ-PAW-086 - ASR: Block Office communication application from creating child processes for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-communication-child-processes-md)**
12. **[REQ-PAW-087 - ASR: Block persistence through WMI event subscription for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md)**
13. **[REQ-PAW-088 - ASR: Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md)**
14. **[REQ-PAW-089 - ASR: Block untrusted and unsigned processes that run from USB for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md)**
15. **[REQ-PAW-090 - ASR: Block Win32 API calls from Office macros for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-block-win32-api-calls-from-office-macros-md)**
16. **[REQ-PAW-091 - ASR: Use advanced protection against ransomware for PAWs](#07-paws-defender-asr-use-advanced-protection-against-ransomware-md)**

---

* **ANSSI Active Directory Hardening Guide**: Protective controls baselines on Privileged Access Workstations

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md"></div>

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-req-paw-076-asr-block-abuse-of-exploited-vulnerable-signed-drivers-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-076] ASR: Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `56a863a9-875e-4185-98a7-b882c64b5ce5` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Prevents an application from writing a vulnerable signed driver to disk. Attackers use Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) techniques to bypass Windows kernel protections by loading legitimate, signed third-party drivers that contain known vulnerabilities, allowing them to disable security agents and gain kernel-level privileges.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Administrators or developers who deliberately load older or specific signed debugging/hardware diagnostics drivers containing known security bugs will be blocked. Approvals or exclusions must be configured for these specific drivers.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-vulnerable-signed-drivers-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction
2. Set 'Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules' to 'Enabled'

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-req-paw-077-asr-block-adobe-reader-from-creating-child-processes-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-077] ASR: Block Adobe Reader from creating child processes for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `7674ba52-37eb-4a4f-a9a1-f0f9a1619a2c` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Prevents Adobe Reader from launching any child processes. Malicious PDF documents frequently attempt to exploit application vulnerabilities or trick users into executing embedded links, which spawns command shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or scripting hosts (wscript.exe) to download and launch secondary malware payloads.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Adobe Reader will be unable to launch external helper applications directly. PDF forms that rely on spawning external applications or customized plugins that execute command-line helpers will fail to run.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-adobe-reader-child-processes-md-implementation-steps"></div>

3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `7674ba52-37eb-4a4f-a9a1-f0f9a1619a2c` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md-req-paw-078-asr-block-all-office-applications-from-creating-child-processes-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-078] ASR: Block all Office applications from creating child processes for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `d4f940ab-401b-4efc-aadc-ad5f3c50688a` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Blocks Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) from creating child processes. This prevents malicious files containing embedded VBA macros or exploiting unpatched vulnerabilities (such as CVE-2021-40444) from launching scripting environments or system commands to download and execute code.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Office macros that legitimately launch external scripts, shell scripts, or third-party executable helpers will be blocked. Business processes relying on advanced inter-process macros must be rewritten to use modern API alternatives.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-child-processes-md-implementation-steps"></div>

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md"></div>

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-req-paw-079-asr-block-credential-stealing-from-the-windows-local-security-authority-subsystem-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-079] ASR: Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Blocks attempts to open or dump the memory of the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (lsass.exe). Attackers dump LSASS memory using tools like Mimikatz or Task Manager to extract plaintext credentials, Kerberos tickets, or NTLM password hashes from system memory for lateral movement.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Administrative diagnostic tools, customized authentication packages, or security scanners that attempt to open the LSASS process handle to read user tokens or perform access auditing will be blocked.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-lsass-credential-stealing-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md-req-paw-080-asr-block-executable-content-from-email-client-and-webmail-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-080] ASR: Block executable content from email client and webmail for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `be9ba2d9-53ea-4cdc-84e5-9b1eeee46550` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Prevents executable files (such as .exe, .com, .scr, .vbs, .js, or .pif) from launching directly from email clients (like Outlook) or webmail accessed via browser sessions. This stops phishing attacks where users accidentally launch malicious attachments or download payloads directly from web-based email links.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Users will be blocked from directly launching attachments that contain scripts, setup files, or macros. They must first save the file to an authorized directory and run it from there (which allows standard real-time scans to run first).

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-email-executable-content-md-implementation-steps"></div>

# [REQ-PAW-081] ASR: Block executable files from running unless they meet a prevalence, age, or trusted list criterion for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-low-prevalence-executable-files-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-low-prevalence-executable-files-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `01443614-cd74-433a-b99e-2ecdc07bfc25` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-low-prevalence-executable-files-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Blocks execution of unrecognized, newly compiled, or low-prevalence executable files. This provides initial protection against zero-day malware campaigns and targeted custom payloads that have not yet established reputation telemetry in the Microsoft Cloud Protection network.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-low-prevalence-executable-files-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>

Developers building and testing custom internal binaries, or administrators installing niche, uncertified third-party software updates will face false positives. Exclusions must be configured for target test directories.

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md-req-paw-082-asr-block-execution-of-potentially-obfuscated-scripts-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-082] ASR: Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `5beb7efe-fd9a-4556-801d-275e5ffc04cc` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Blocks execution of obfuscated or encrypted scripts (such as PowerShell, VBScript, or JavaScript). Threat actors obfuscate their scripts using base64 encoding, custom string manipulation, or encryption to hide the intent of their code and bypass static file scanning and network detection engines.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Legitimate administrative tools or third-party provisioning scripts that use heavy minification, obfuscation, or custom encoding wrappers will be blocked. Scripts must be refactored to use readable, signed code.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction
2. Set 'Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules' to 'Enabled'
3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `5beb7efe-fd9a-4556-801d-275e5ffc04cc` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-obfuscated-scripts-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)
[Download Script: Configure-PawAsrObfuscatedScripts.ps1](../../implementation_scripts/Configure-PawAsrObfuscatedScripts.ps1)

```powershell
# Configure-PawAsrObfuscatedScripts.ps1
$AsrRulesPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules"
if (-not (Test-Path $AsrRulesPath)) { New-Item -Path $AsrRulesPath -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $AsrRulesPath -Name "5beb7efe-fd9a-4556-801d-275e5ffc04cc" -Value "1" -Type String -Force
```

*To audit the hardening status:*
[Download Script: Get-PawAsrObfuscatedScriptsStatus.ps1](../../audit_scripts/Get-PawAsrObfuscatedScriptsStatus.ps1)

```powershell
# Get-PawAsrObfuscatedScriptsStatus.ps1
$AsrRulesPath = "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules"
$Value = Get-ItemProperty -Path $AsrRulesPath -Name "5beb7efe-fd9a-4556-801d-275e5ffc04cc" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($Value -and ($Value."5beb7efe-fd9a-4556-801d-275e5ffc04cc" -eq "1" -or $Value."5beb7efe-fd9a-4556-801d-275e5ffc04cc" -eq 1)) {
    Write-Output "Compliant"
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Output "Non-Compliant"
    exit 1
}
```

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-script-launching-downloaded-content-md-req-paw-083-asr-block-javascript-or-vbscript-from-launching-downloaded-executable-content-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-083] ASR: Block JavaScript or VBScript from launching downloaded executable content for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-script-launching-downloaded-content-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-script-launching-downloaded-content-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `d3e037e1-3eb8-44c8-a917-57927947596d` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-script-launching-downloaded-content-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Prevents JavaScript or VBScript running locally from launching executable binaries that were downloaded from the internet. Attackers use malicious scripts inside documents or web browsers to download payloads (like ransomware or trojans) to the disk and launch them using local script engines.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-script-launching-downloaded-content-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Local administrative script engines that perform software deployment or download updates and then launch installers will be blocked. These scripts must be replaced by structured configuration agents or signed installers.

---

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty -Path $AsrRulesPath -Name "d3e037e1-3eb8-44c8-a917-57927947596d" -Value "1" -Type String -Force
```

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-executable-content-creation-md-req-paw-084-asr-block-office-applications-from-creating-executable-content-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-084] ASR: Block Office applications from creating executable content for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-executable-content-creation-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-executable-content-creation-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `3b576869-a4ec-4529-8536-b80a7769e899` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-executable-content-creation-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Prevents Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) from creating or writing executable files (e.g., .exe, .dll, .scr) to the local filesystem. Malicious documents often attempt to drop payloads directly into the local temp folders or AppData directories before executing them.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-executable-content-creation-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Macros or add-ins that legitimately save external binaries or compile executable helper objects locally will be blocked.

---

3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `3b576869-a4ec-4529-8536-b80a7769e899` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

# [REQ-PAW-085] ASR: Block Office applications from injecting code into other processes for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-code-injection-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-code-injection-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `75668c1f-73b5-4cf0-bb93-3ecf5cb7cc84` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-code-injection-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Blocks Microsoft Office applications from writing code or injecting threads directly into external processes. Threat actors use code injection (such as process hollowing or remote thread creation) inside Office macros to hide execution under clean, trusted system binaries like explorer.exe or svchost.exe.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-code-injection-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Office plugins or custom integration tools that inject threads or communicate with database engines using active injection libraries will be blocked.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-communication-child-processes-md-req-paw-086-asr-block-office-communication-application-from-creating-child-processes-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-086] ASR: Block Office communication application from creating child processes for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-communication-child-processes-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-communication-child-processes-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `26190899-1602-49e8-8b27-eb1d0a1ce869` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-communication-child-processes-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Blocks Microsoft Outlook or other Office communication applications (e.g., Teams, Skype) from creating child processes. This prevents malware payloads delivered through emails, chats, or calendar invites from spawning command-line utilities or scripting environments.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-office-communication-child-processes-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Outlook integrations or custom add-ins that legitimately spawn helper utilities, such as starting external browsers or custom document handlers directly, may be blocked.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-req-paw-087-asr-block-persistence-through-wmi-event-subscription-for-paws"></div>
# [REQ-PAW-087] ASR: Block persistence through WMI event subscription for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `e6db77e5-3df2-4cf1-b95a-636979351e5b` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Blocks threat actors from achieving system persistence by registering permanent Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) event subscriptions. WMI event subscriptions allow attackers to automatically launch malicious payloads when system triggers occur (like system boot or user logon) without using traditional startup registry keys.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Management software or diagnostic monitoring tools that legitimately register permanent WMI event filters to track system telemetry will be blocked. Alternatives like Windows services or scheduled tasks must be used.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction
2. Set 'Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules' to 'Enabled'
3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `e6db77e5-3df2-4cf1-b95a-636979351e5b` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-wmi-event-subscription-persistence-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>
### Option B: PowerShell & Registry Configuration (Remediation / Non-GPO)

# [REQ-PAW-088] ASR: Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `d1e49aac-8f56-4280-b9ba-993a6d77406c` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Blocks processes created via WMI commands or PSExec remote execution utilities. This directly stops lateral movement attacks where compromised accounts or threat actors attempt to start commands, backdoors, or credential dumpers remotely across domain-joined servers and PAW platforms.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Disrupts remote administration tools, monitoring agents, and network scanners that rely on WMI/PSExec. For Domain Controllers or critical servers, this rule is often set to **Audit** mode (`2`) rather than hard Block mode (`1`) to prevent administrative downtime.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>
### Option A: Group Policy Object (GPO) Configuration (Preferred)
1. Navigate to: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction
2. Set 'Configure Attack Surface Reduction rules' to 'Enabled'
3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `d1e49aac-8f56-4280-b9ba-993a6d77406c` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-psexec-wmi-process-creations-md-option-b-powershell-registry-configuration-remediation-non-gpo"></div>

```powershell
Set-ItemProperty -Path $AsrRulesPath -Name "d1e49aac-8f56-4280-b9ba-993a6d77406c" -Value "1" -Type String -Force
```

# [REQ-PAW-089] ASR: Block untrusted and unsigned processes that run from USB for PAWs

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md-target-scope"></div>
## Target Scope
* **Applicable Systems**: Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) used for Tier 0 directory administration.
* **Operating Systems**: Windows 10 Enterprise (1607+) and Windows 11 Enterprise.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md-implementation-details"></div>
## Implementation Details
* **Priority**: High
* **GPO Path / Registry Location**:
  * **GPO Path**: `Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Defender Antivirus\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\Attack Surface Reduction`
  * **Registry Location**:
    * `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\ASR\Rules`
      * `b2b3f03d-6a65-4f7b-a9c7-1c7ef74a9ba4` = `1` (REG_SZ)

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md-rationale"></div>
## Rationale
Blocks the execution of unsigned or untrusted processes on removable storage devices (USB drives, external SSDs). This stops physical access vectors, rogue USB drops, and automated worm propagation techniques from running unauthorized installers or scripts.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md-legacy-impact-compatibility"></div>
## Legacy Impact & Compatibility
Administrators or developers will be unable to run unsigned utilities directly from portable flash drives. Software must be copied to local trusted storage, or the binary must possess a trusted digital signature.

---

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md-implementation-steps"></div>
## Implementation Steps

<div id="07-paws-defender-asr-block-unsigned-processes-running-from-usb-md-option-a-group-policy-object-gpo-configuration-preferred"></div>

3. Click 'Show...' and add the rule GUID `b2b3f03d-6a65-4f7b-a9c7-1c7ef74a9ba4` as Value Name, with Value set to `1` (Block).

---
